resources.level: intermediate to advanced (for solvers moving from 4a/4b to full EOLR)
resources.summary: A one-tab Google Doc of about 14.7k characters, exported as text and HTML. It has no images and no links. The Roux Reader link ends in a stray ']' (%5D), which returns 404; the plain /edit URL returns 200. The doc teaches every EOLR case (EO plus the UL/UR edges) as an intuitive procedure, not as algs. Its outline follows the EO groups: Arrow, 1F-1B, 4-0, 2LR-2, 2FB-0, 0-2, 2BL-0, 2BL-2 and 4-2. In the names, X-Y means X bad edges on U and Y on D; FB/LR means an opposite pair and BL an adjacent pair. Each group is split into named sub-cases ranked from best to worst: Best, Good, Great, Alright, Decent, Stack, Adjacent, Bottom, Quick EO, 'UF is LR', Bad, Worst. The doc says the top cases matter most. Each sub-case lists the L/R placements it covers as position pairs such as UFDF or ULDB, gives one setup alg (one sub-case has three), and explains the solution in prose. Almost every solution reduces the case to one of 5 arrow sub-cases (Best, Good, Adjacent, Bottom, Bad), usually with an 'M, U, undo the M' pattern. A few cases instead go straight to EO and then 4b, or to 4c. Solutions may end with misoriented centres. The doc also points out links between groups: 2LR-2 is 4-0 after an M2, 2BL-0 cases match 2BL-2 cases without the bottom bad edges, and 1F-1B DFDB is the 'M2-adjusted brother' of UFUB. Two groups are left unwritten. 2LR-2 says 'refer to 4-0' and admits it should be written out. 4-2 (6-flip) says to look up GuRoux's 6-flip videos on YouTube. In total there are 40 sub-cases covering 104 placements; 0-2 lists 14 placements instead of 15, and ULUR is missing.

resources.title: Optimal EOLR (linked as 'Optimal EOLR Spreadsheet')
resources.author: Not stated in the sheet. Every solved row links to a timestamp in John Mark Grimes's YouTube EOLR series (11 videos, from 'Full EOLR | Best Guide - Ep. 1' through Ep. 8½, plus '6-Flip EOLRb made Easy'; authors confirmed via YouTube oEmbed). It is very likely his companion sheet, but this is unconfirmed.
resources.summary: A single-tab sheet ('Cases', gid 1330121609), saved as CSV, xlsx (with formulas) and htmlview. It holds 64 case rows and 2 footer rows. The columns are: Case Name, EO Symmetries, LR Symmetries, AUF angles (1, 2 or 4 distinct pre-AUFs), Movecount (a formula counting M moves; values 1-11 STM), a Misoriented Centers flag, an AUF Trick flag, Image, Setup, an Intermediary Cell, Solution, an 'AUF trick' alternative, Video Link, Movecount + AUF, Probability, weighted, and Symmetries. Images are visualcube.api.cubing.net IMAGE() formulas with an LSE sticker mask. The Solution column is computed from the setup by regexreplace formulas: it is the inverse of the setup, so solution and setup are a single alg. Case names follow one system: the EO group (3/1 arrow, 1/1, 4/0, 0/2, 2o/0, 2a/0, 2o/2, 2a/2, 4/2 and 0/0, where 'o' means opposite and 'a' means adjacent for 2 bad top edges), then the orientation of the L and R edges (MM both misoriented, OM one of each, OO both oriented, M/O and O/M for which is on top), then their placement (adj or opp on U, 'both' for one on U and one on D, D for both on D). The arrow group instead uses the names Best, Good, Mediocre and D Arrow. 53 rows are fully filled with setup, solution and video timestamp. 29 of them end with misoriented centres, and 10 have an AUF-trick alternative. A trailing block of 7 '3/1' rows (one name duplicated) and 4 '0/0' (EO-solved) rows has only weights and movecounts: no setup, solution or video. The arrow weights may therefore be counted twice in the total, which is 496 symmetry units. Footer: the weighted average EOLR movecount including pre-AUF is 5.63 STM, against 7.38 STM for inserting UL/UR in step 4b. There is no prose, no recognition guide and no licence.

resources.title: Advanced CEOR (linked as 'CEOR (to do CPFB instead of FB, and COLS instead of SBLP)')
resources.author: CubeAlgs101 made the sheet, 'with help from MikeZB and additional algs from USBB' (Info tab). The credit cells link to the YouTube channels @cubealgs101, @Mike_zb and @ulrikbredland6965.
resources.summary:
A large sheet for CEOR, a CP-first one-handed method that is NOT Roux. Its steps are: CPLine (a 1x1x3 bar at DL with corner permutation solved), then CPFB, then EO plus the DF/DB edges, then a right block with <R,U>, then 2GLL; the sheet gives 45-55 moves. The workbook has 26 tabs: 24 visible and 2 hidden ('LXS (Back)', 'EOPair'). The htmlview lists only the visible ones, so the hidden tabs were read from the xlsx. The xlsx is 26.8 MB with 1,400 embedded images: custom 3D cube renders with grey CP-tracing stickers. Many cells carry notes, which are alternative algs or mnemonics. Tab colours mark the steps; the Info tab says pink tabs are 'extra and not part of CEOR'. Each alg tab opens with 'Total Cases = N // Average Moves = X' and has colour legends (green 2-gen, red 3-gen, yellow non-intuitive; or green 'necessary to learn').
Of all this, only the CP tools apply to the Roux family: the CPLine/CPFB tab and the 'Tracking F Moves' mnemonics. These fit CP-first Roux (RUroux/CPRoux), which the Resources tab cross-links (Edde's sheet). The 2-gen pair, slot and square sets assume EO and DF/DB already solved, so they carry over to Roux SB only partly. Everything else is out of scope for a Roux-only app: EO+DF/DB, Stripe, 2GLL, 2GR, Nautilus, APB and MI1. The hub text 'COLS instead of SBLP' has no matching tab; the nearest are Last Slot and Multislot.
The Resources tab links: the CEOR Discord; the CEOR Tutorial and CEOR Mega Doc (Google Docs); the CEOR Trainer (edde.github.io/CEORtrainer); the RUroux/CPRoux spreadsheet; Ulrik's CP Tracing (UCPT); and 3 sheets (CEOR Swap Pairs, CEOR Solving Corner Permutation, CP tracking F moves). 'Tracking F Moves' also links a visualiser at mike-zb.github.io/F-MovesTracking.

resources.title: Roux movecount stats (linked as 'Movecount statistics' in the Roux Reader blockbuilding chapter)
resources.author: onionhoney: 'For any questions / requests please contact @onionhoney in RMS discord.' onionhoney is the author of the upstream Roux Trainers.
resources.level: advanced (method analysis); the headline numbers work as benchmarks at any level
resources.summary: A statistics workbook with 6 tabs, all visible: FB, FB Appendix, SB, LSE, 4c and 4c-detail. It contains no algs. FB tab (implicitly HTM): average moves and cumulative distributions from 100k simulations for an FB square (fixed 3.96, y 3.23, x2y 2.86, CN 2.67; a fixed square is 4.36), the FB last pair (4.08), the full FB (fixed 6.70, y 5.96, x2y 5.60, CN 5.14) and FB + DR edge in HTM (7.64 / 6.93 / 6.59 / 6.14) and in QTM. Short comments note, for example, that going from x2y to full CN raises the share of FBs in 5 moves or fewer from 0.38 to 0.69. FB Appendix is one screenshot of an exhaustive solver run: FB fixed, 5,322,240 cases, average 6.700925, full length distribution. SB tab: the front second-block square (SS, counted solved only when every piece is placed) in STM with <R,r,U,M> and with <U,D,F,B,R,r,M>. Results are split by DR state (all 6.78; DR oriented 6.45; misoriented 7.11; misoriented and not in M 7.45) and by DR and FR position (18 positions each, 6.35 to 7.68). Back SS is said to be symmetric. LSE tab (<M,U>, STM): LSE 11.14 (exact), L5E 11.08, ELL 11.54, EO-solved LSE 8.57 ('Solving EO during CMLL saves a lot of moves'), and EOLR or EOLR+FB (EOBF), with and without misoriented centres, to 'place at dfdb' (5.97-7.67) and to finish (12.78-14.00). Some of these are marked 'yet to be verified', and an 'old data that's likely wrong' section follows. Conclusions given: the EOLR/FB family averages only about 1.3 moves above optimal, EOFB saves almost a move, and EOLRFB may beat EOLR+MC. 4c tab: 4c after EOLR (pending pre-AUF and M2) in STM and SQTM over {M,U} for EOLR and EOBF, non-MC and MC (6.63-7.23 STM), and after EOLRb/EOBFb (5.00-5.67 STM). 4c-detail has an empty table and 16 solver screenshots, one per group (48-case EOLRb/EOBFb groups and 192-case 4c groups for ULUR/UFUB aligned or misaligned, each with average and distribution).
